The hearings in the instant matter were held on 29.5.2025 and 19.8.2025, and the order was reserved. This order is passed considering the Petitioner’s submissions in the Petition vide affidavit dated 29 .7.2024, and the subsequent affidavits dated 8.7.2025 and 2.9.2025 . Further, Respondent No. 1, i.e., Bihar State Power (Holding) Company Limited (BSPHCL), filed its reply vide affidavit dated 5.8.2025, to which the Petitioner filed its rejoinder vide affidavit dated 19.8.2025. The issues raised by BSHPCL and the clarifications furnished by the Petitioner thereon have been considered in the subsequent paragraphs of this order. 8. Having heard the learned counsel of the BSHPCL and the representatives of the Petitioner and having perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the instant Petition in the succeeding paragraphs. placed on record. It is observed that in support of its claim of COD of the instant communication assets, the Petitioner has submitted the RLDC Energisation Certificates 32. Respondent No. 1, i.e., Bihar State Power Holding Company Limited (BSPHCL), vide affidavit dated 5.8.2025, has submitted that the Petitioner has claimed the increase in completion cost _, inter alia_ , to the increase in the project implementation period due to delay in execution of the links. It has further submitted that the delay in time overrun are attributable to the Petitioner, and therefore, cannot be condoned for the reasons stated in the instant Petition. Any cost escalation arising from such delay should not be passed on to the beneficiaries and should be borne by the Petitioner. 52. BSPHCL has contended that the Petitioner has failed to demonstrate any proactive or timely follow-up with OPTCL. It has submitted that, except for two letters dated 12.12.2017 and 8.5.2018, the Petitioner has furnished no documentary evidence to establish continuous engagement or escalation of the matter. The record shows that the Petitioner's follow-up was inadequate and that it took no tangible steps to expedite the availability of the work front. Accordingly, the Petitioner has failed to establish that the entire period of 1005 days of delay was beyond its control. It has further submitted that, out of the total delay of 1699 days claimed by the Petitioner for Asset-I, it has provided no justification for the 694-day delay during the period from April 2014 to July 2016. Accordingly, the BSPHCL has contended that the Petitioner has failed to make out a case for condonation of the delay in commissioning of Asset-I. 55. The Respondent has submitted that the Petitioner has failed to provide any justification for the remaining 1689 days of delay beyond the SCOD. Accordingly, the said delay is not condonable. 59. BSPHCL has submitted that the Petitioner has failed to provide any explanation 60. The Petitioner, in its rejoinder vide affidavit dated 19.8.2025, has submitted the reasons for the time overrun with respect to the communication assets, which have already been elaborated in the Petition and are supported by documentary evidence. 62. The Petitioner is entitled to reimbursement of the fees paid for filing the Petition and publication expenses incurred on this account directly from the beneficiaries or long-term customers, as the case may be in accordance with Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 132.
